unimportable_by_construction.finding: H-3 / defect class O10, ratified 21 July 2026 as N-23.
unimportable_by_construction.how_asserted: STATICALLY, via the AST, NEVER by importing. Importing connectivity_buildup.py under Colab succeeds on 'from google.colab import drive' and then blocks on drive.mount(force_remount=True), executing the notebook body as a side effect (see s06 asserted_statically_not_by_importing). test_s0_import_surface.py loads the blockers from the S0.6 declaration named above -- one source of truth -- and asserts each is still present. A file that starts importing means the O10 assignment (N-23) needs revisiting: the declaration is then stale, which is an error, not good news.
unimportable_by_construction.assignment: S1/S3 with the exporter-pinning work (N-23). Not S0.

absent_runtime_dependency.finding: New at S0.9, measured, not previously narrated. These modules are importable in principle -- their own surface is sound -- but import third-party scientific packages that a clean checkout does not install, because pyproject.toml declares zero runtime dependencies by decision (until B-4 is answered).
absent_runtime_dependency.policy: For every package module NOT in the unimportable_by_construction set and NOT in known_absent_dependency_modules below, importlib.import_module MUST succeed, OR it may fail ONLY with ModuleNotFoundError whose missing top-level package is (a) not in the standard library, (b) not a towards_eeg submodule, and (c) not a declared runtime dependency of towards_eeg (pyproject [project].dependencies). Any other failure -- SyntaxError, NameError, an ImportError that is not this gated ModuleNotFoundError, a missing towards_eeg submodule, or a missing DECLARED runtime dependency -- is a real FAIL. The gate is self-verifying against pyproject: the day a package is declared a runtime dependency, its absence stops excusing an import failure.

known_absent_dependency_modules.note: The heavy simulator modules. Asserted STATICALLY (like O10) rather than imported, because importing driver.py in an environment where NEURON IS present would run NEURON/MPI initialisation as a side effect. The assertion is a staleness guard: each still imports at least one non-stdlib, non-towards_eeg, non-declared-runtime top-level package at module scope. If one becomes plainly importable, this declaration is flagged stale.

A NEW duplicate is not exempt and fails.

ledger_reconstruction_exemptions.assertion: 8 -- every tracked file reconstructs byte-identically from its recorded ledger hashes.
ledger_reconstruction_exemptions.reason: These three ARE the record. Their on-disk bytes include hashes that are computed from their own content, so a regeneration re-measures a file the previous regeneration just rewrote; their current-hash columns necessarily float by one generation and cannot equal a column they help produce. Every OTHER tracked, non-discard file must hash to its end-of-chain column; every discard file must be absent with its last hash preserved in s07_discard_manifest.json (reusing the tools/test_s0_chain.py half-A logic).

pyproject_still_declares_no_dependencies.statement: S0.9 does NOT add pytest to pyproject.toml [project].dependencies, and does NOT add [project.optional-dependencies]. The runtime dependency list stays empty, so the pending zero-runtime-dependencies decision is left undisturbed and 'pip install towards_eeg' still pulls nothing.
pyproject_still_declares_no_dependencies.how_pytest_is_declared_instead: requirements/dev.txt (new file, clause 3), consistent with the existing requirements/ convention (hybrid_stack.lock). 'pytest passes on a clean checkout' is met by: python3 -m pip install -r requirements/dev.txt && python3 -m pytest tests/.
